text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Bosnian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Bosnian Serb parliament speaker Dragan Kalinic accused president Biljana Plavsic of "revealing state secrets" by submitting documents on smuggling deals in the Serb entity, Serb agencies report.
- International High Representative to Bosnia Carlos Westendorp officially confirmed that Jacques Klein, current UNTAES head, has been named as one of his two deputies.

- Prime minister of the Moslem-Croat federation Edhem Bicakcic says donors' conference, expected to be held in July, may be postponed until September due to summer holidays in Europe. Bicakcic says this will cause a delay in reconstruction projects.

- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic, replying to accusations by the Serb Democratic Party (SDS), said the party leadership had expected her to be a puppet in the hands of former president and indicted war criminal Radovan Karadzic.
- Head of Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) mission to Bosnia Robert Frowick said his organisation supports Plavsic as the legally elected president of the Serb entity.
- President of Slovenian Association of Trade Unions Dusan Semolic says the union will propose the Slovenian government abolish visas for Bosnians.
- The opposition Union of Bosnian Social Democrats demands the federation interior ministry reveal all details of possible deals between Bosnian Serb authorities and Sarajevo mafia during the war.

- President of the Moslem-Croat federation Vladimir Soljic, when asked about alleged smuggling links between the Serb entity and the federation, said "there is no war without criminals". -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
